765	    def _recover_pending_events(self) -> None:
766	        """Commit outbox events left pending by a crashed process."""
767	        try:
768	            names = os.listdir(self.data_dir)
769	        except OSError:
770	            return
771	        for name in names:
772	            if not (name.endswith(".json") and is_valid_key_id(name[:-5])):
773	                continue

797	                    continue

800	                    # minted handles are now owned by the key, so the
801	                    # attempt's provision journal is finished.

804	    def _commit_mutation(
805	        self,
806	        path: str,
807	        record: KeyRecord,
808	        event: AuditEvent,
809	        previous: Optional[dict],
810	        provider=None,
811	        new_handles=(),
812	        journal_id: Optional[str] = None,
813	        pre_commit=None,
814	    ) -> None:
815	        """Commit a key-file change and its event as one logical transaction.
816	
817	        The record is first written carrying the pending event (an outbox
818	        marker), the event is then appended durably to the ledger, and the
819	        marker is cleared in a second atomic write. If the ledger append
820	        fails the key file is rolled back (deleted for a brand-new key whose
821	        ``previous`` is None, restored to its prior bytes otherwise), and any
822	        provider handles the change minted are deleted, so a failed ledger
823	        write leaves neither a single-sided file nor an orphaned HSM object.
824	        ``journal_id`` (import only) is folded into the marker so crash
825	        recovery can drop the attempt's provision journal after resolving it.
826	        ``pre_commit`` (when given) runs strictly between the durable marker
827	        write and the ledger append: it lets the caller durably persist the
828	        idempotent operation's terminal context so the response can be
829	        replayed verbatim once the event lands; an exception rolls the file
830	        and handles back exactly like a failed ledger append. A crash at any
831	        point is repaired idempotently by _recover_pending_events on the next
832	        open.
833	        """
834	        marker = event.to_json()
835	        if journal_id:
836	            marker = dict(marker)
837	            marker["journal"] = journal_id
838	        record.pending_event = marker
839	
840	        def release_handles() -> bool:
841	            # Returns False when a minted handle could not be deleted: the
842	            # caller must surface that (503) instead of hiding an orphaned
843	            # backend object.
844	            if provider is None:
845	                return True
846	            cleaned = True
847	            for handle in new_handles:
848	                try:
849	                    provider.delete(handle)
850	                except Exception:
851	                    cleaned = False
852	            return cleaned
853	
854	        try:
855	            self._write_atomic(path, record.to_json())
856	            if pre_commit is not None:
857	                # The in-memory record already carries the version being
858	                # committed, so the caller can stage the exact 201 response
859	                # before the commit-point append.
860	                pre_commit(record)
861	            self.audit.append(event)
862	        except BaseException as exc:
863	            # Only roll the file back when it may have landed: a failure of
864	            # the ledger append, or of the initial write after a partial file.
865	            if os.path.exists(path):
866	                if previous is None:
867	                    try:
868	                        os.unlink(path)
869	                    except OSError:
870	                        pass
871	                else:
872	                    try:
873	                        self._write_atomic(path, previous)
874	                    except Exception:
875	                        pass
876	            if not release_handles():
877	                # The file is rolled back but a backend object survives:
878	                # report a provider failure (503, generic client message);
879	                # callers keep/retry the provision journal so startup
880	                # eventually deletes the handle.
881	                raise ProviderUnavailable(
882	                    "rollback could not delete a provisioned provider handle"
883	                ) from exc
884	            raise
885	        # The durable ledger append is the commit point: the change and its
886	        # event are now authoritative and must never be rolled back. Clearing
887	        # the marker is best-effort housekeeping; a failure here (or a crash)
888	        # is repaired on the next open and must not surface as a failed
889	        # request or trigger handle deletion.
890	        record.pending_event = None
891	        try:
892	            self._write_atomic(path, record.to_json())
893	        except OSError:
894	            pass

910	    @contextmanager
911	    def _timed_inproc(self, key_id: str, deadline) -> Iterator[None]:
912	        """Acquire the per-key in-process lock against a shared deadline."""
913	        inproc = self._key_lock(key_id)
914	        remaining = max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)
915	        if not inproc.acquire(timeout=remaining):
916	            raise LockTimeout(key_id)
917	        try:
918	            yield
919	        finally:
920	            inproc.release()

922	    @contextmanager
923	    def _file_lock(self, key_id: str, deadline=None) -> Iterator[None]:
924	        """Cross-process advisory lock guarding mutation of a single key.
925	
926	        The in-process lock is taken separately by callers. With ``deadline``
927	        (a monotonic deadline) the fcntl lock is acquired non-blocking with
928	        polling and :class:`LockTimeout` is raised when the deadline passes;
929	        otherwise this blocks until acquired, the historical behavior.
930	        """
931	        lock_path = self._lock_path_for(key_id)
932	        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
933	            yield
934	            return
935	        fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
936	        acquired = False
937	        try:
938	            if deadline is None:
939	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
940	            else:
941	                while True:
942	                    try:
943	                        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
944	                        break
945	                    except BlockingIOError:
946	                        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
947	                        if remaining <= 0:
948	                            raise LockTimeout(key_id)
949	                        time.sleep(min(0.02, remaining))
950	            acquired = True
951	            yield
952	        finally:
953	            if acquired:
954	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
955	            os.close(fd)

960	        The temp file is fsynced before the rename, so a crash at any point
961	        leaves either the previous file or the complete new file.
962	        """
963	        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=self.data_dir, suffix=".tmp")
964	        try:

966	                json.dump(payload, fh)
967	                fh.flush()
968	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
969	            os.chmod(tmp_path, 0o600)
970	            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
971	        except BaseException:
972	            try:
973	                os.unlink(tmp_path)
974	            except OSError:
975	                pass

1015	    def create(self, tenant_id: str, algorithm: str, label: str) -> KeyRecord:

1019	        triple (provider_id, handle, encrypted_material) is persisted. The
1020	        create event is committed in the same transaction as the key file; a
1021	        ledger failure deletes both the just-written file and the minted
1022	        handle and raises LedgerError, so the change and its event never land
1023	        separately.
1024	        """

1028	        created_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
1029	        record = KeyRecord(
1030	            key_id=key_id,
1031	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1032	            label=label,
1033	            versions=[
1034	                VersionRecord(
1035	                    version=1,
1036	                    created_at=created_at,
1037	                    algorithm=algorithm,
1038	                    public_key=triple.public_key,
1039	                    provider_id=provider.provider_id,
1040	                    handle=triple.handle,
1041	                    encrypted_material=triple.encrypted_material,
1042	                )
1043	            ],
1044	            current_version=1,
1045	        )

1047	            tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_CREATE, key_id,
1048	            audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS, timestamp=created_at,
1049	        )

1070	    def rotate(
1071	        self,
1072	        key_id: str,
1073	        tenant_id: str,
1074	        algorithm: str,
1075	        event_id: Optional[str] = None,
1076	        lock_timeout: Optional[float] = None,
1077	        pre_commit=None,
1078	    ) -> Optional[KeyRecord]:
1079	        """Append a new version with fresh material.
1080	
1081	        Returns None for an unknown or foreign key. Versions are strictly
1082	        incrementing; the on-disk state is read, extended and written back
1083	        atomically under per-key locks so concurrent rotations never lose a
1084	        version or leave a dangling current pointer.
1085	
1086	        An idempotent operation supplies ``event_id`` (its operation_id, so a
1087	        retried/crashed rotation dedupes on one id) and ``lock_timeout``: if
1088	        the per-key lock cannot be taken within it, :class:`LockTimeout` is
1089	        raised before any provider call or write.
1090	        """
1091	        if not _KEY_ID_RE.fullmatch(key_id):
1092	            return None
1093	        path = self._path_for(key_id)
1094	        with self.key_locks(key_id, timeout=lock_timeout):
1095	            record = self._read_record(path)
1096	            if record is None or record.tenant_id != tenant_id:
1097	                return None
1098	            # A version is rotated on the provider that owns the record;
1099	            # switching providers mid-key is refused (503), never silently
1100	            # migrated.
1101	            provider = self._provider_for(record.current.provider_id)
1102	            previous = record.to_json()
1103	            # Mint the committing event and its provision journal *before*
1104	            # the provider call: a crash after the backend mints the new
1105	            # version's handle but before the commit point is reaped at the
1106	            # next open exactly like an import (event absent -> handle
1107	            # deleted, key file left at its prior version).
1108	            next_number = record.current_version + 1
1109	            created_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
1110	            event = self.audit.new_event(
1111	                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_ROTATE, key_id,
1112	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS, timestamp=created_at,
1113	                event_id=event_id,
1114	            )
1115	            journal_id, journal_path = self._new_provision_journal(
1116	                event.event_id
1117	            )
1118	            minted_handle = None
1119	            try:
1120	                triple = provider.rotate(algorithm)
1121	                minted_handle = triple.handle
1122	                self._append_provision(
1123	                    journal_path, provider.provider_id, triple.handle
1124	                )
1125	                record.append_version(
1126	                    VersionRecord(
1127	                        version=next_number,
1128	                        created_at=created_at,
1129	                        algorithm=algorithm,
1130	                        public_key=triple.public_key,
1131	                        provider_id=provider.provider_id,
1132	                        handle=triple.handle,
1133	                        encrypted_material=triple.encrypted_material,
1134	                    )
1135	                )
1136	                # _commit_mutation deletes the minted handle itself when the
1137	                # append fails; the provision journal is the durable crash
1138	                # safety net and is retried below on any failure.
1139	                self._commit_mutation(
1140	                    path, record, event, previous,
1141	                    provider=provider, new_handles=(triple.handle,),
1142	                    journal_id=journal_id,
1143	                    pre_commit=pre_commit,
1144	                )
1145	            except BaseException as exc:
1146	                # Provider fault, validation or ledger/write failure: the
1147	                # version never committed. Delete the in-memory handle
1148	                # directly and reconcile the durable journal (idempotent
1149	                # deletes). If the backend delete cannot be verified the
1150	                # journal stays for the next open and the request answers 503
1151	                # rather than hiding an orphaned backend object.
1152	                cleaned = True
1153	                if minted_handle is not None:
1154	                    try:
1155	                        provider.delete(minted_handle)
1156	                    except Exception:
1157	                        cleaned = False
1158	                if not self.rollback_provision_journal(journal_id):
1159	                    cleaned = False
1160	                if not cleaned:
1161	                    raise ProviderUnavailable(
1162	                        "could not delete a handle provisioned by a failed "
1163	                        "rotation; cleanup will be retried at startup"
1164	                    ) from exc
1165	                raise
1166	            # Committed: the new handle is owned by the appended version and
1167	            # the durable success event makes the journal obsolete.
1168	            self.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)
1169	        return record

1294	    def _adopt_imported_version(self, ver: dict, journal: Optional[str] = None) -> tuple:
1295	        """Adopt one validated bundle version through its target provider.
1296	
1297	        Returns (VersionRecord, provider). A ``provider`` provenance block
1298	        naming the active provider imports through it; a block naming another
1299	        provider is a 503 mismatch. A legacy bundle without a block
1300	        (``keymgr-export-v1`` emitted before the provider layer) is interpreted
1301	        as local material, and is accepted only while the local provider is
1302	        the active one — with an external provider configured it is refused
1303	        503 and never falls back. Only the provider's freshly-minted triple is
1304	        ever persisted; raw private material is never written to a key file.
1305	        Every minted handle is durably recorded in ``journal`` (when given)
1306	        before the call returns, so a crash before the commit point reaps it.
1307	        """
1308	        block = ver.get("provider")
1309	        if block is None:
1310	            if not provider_mod.active_is_local():
1311	                raise ProviderUnavailable(
1312	                    "legacy bundle without a provider block is local-only; "
1313	                    "the local provider is not active"
1314	                )
1315	            target = provider_mod.configure_local(self.data_dir)
1316	        else:
1317	            target = self._provider_for(block["provider_id"])
1318	        triple = target.import_material(
1319	            ver["algorithm"], ver["public_key"], ver["private_material"]
1320	        )
1321	        if journal is not None:
1322	            self._append_provision(journal, target.provider_id, triple.handle)
1323	        public_key = (
1324	            triple.public_key
1325	            if triple.public_key is not None
1326	            else ver["public_key"]
1327	        )
1328	        record = VersionRecord(
1329	            version=ver["version"],
1330	            created_at=ver["created_at"],
1331	            algorithm=ver["algorithm"],
1332	            public_key=public_key,
1333	            provider_id=target.provider_id,
1334	            handle=triple.handle,
1335	            encrypted_material=triple.encrypted_material,
1336	        )
1337	        return record, target

1342	
1343	        Returns True only when every delete succeeded; deletes are idempotent.
1344	        """
1345	        cleaned = True

1353	    def release_record_handles(self, record: KeyRecord) -> bool:
1354	        """Delete every provider handle held by a (discarded) record.
1355	
1356	        Used when a restore that minted provider objects never commits; each
1357	        version is routed to its owning provider. A missing/inactive provider
1358	        means its handles cannot be reached from here, so those versions are
1359	        skipped (the durable journal remains the authoritative retry path);
1360	        only a reachable provider whose delete fails makes this report False.
1361	        """
1362	        cleaned = True
1363	        for ver in record.versions:
1364	            try:
1365	                target = self._provider_for(ver.provider_id)
1366	            except ProviderUnavailable:
1367	                continue
1368	            try:
1369	                target.delete(ver.handle)
1370	            except Exception:
1371	                cleaned = False
1372	        return cleaned

1374	    def import_bundle(
1375	        self,
1376	        tenant_id: str,
1377	        payload: dict,
1378	        event_id: Optional[str] = None,
1379	        lock_timeout: Optional[float] = None,
1380	        pre_commit=None,
1381	    ) -> tuple:
1382	        """Persist a validated export payload under the importing tenant.
1383	
1384	        Returns (IMPORT_CREATED, record) for a brand-new key_id, or
1385	        (IMPORT_CONFLICT, existing) when the key_id already exists; the
1386	        existing record on disk is never touched, and the caller decides 409
1387	        versus 404 from its owner. Every version is adopted through the
1388	        matching provider (a mismatch raises ProviderUnavailable -> 503 and
1389	        malformed material ProviderInvalidMaterial -> 400) **before** the
1390	        conflict recheck or any file is written; handles minted by a refused
1391	        or failed attempt are all deleted and no file or audit line changes.
1392	        A successful import and its audit event commit through the same
1393	        outbox transaction as create/rotate.
1394	
1395	        For an idempotent operation the per-key lock is acquired (with
1396	        ``lock_timeout``) **before** the provision journal or any provider
1397	        handle exists, so a timed-out wait writes no key, audit event or
1398	        handle. ``event_id`` names the committing audit event after the
1399	        operation_id.
1400	        """
1401	        key_id = payload["key_id"]
1402	        # Acquire the key lock first: a lock-wait timeout must surface before
1403	        # a journal, handle or event exists.
1404	        with self.key_locks(key_id, timeout=lock_timeout):
1405	            # Mint the committing event up front so the provision journal is
1406	            # named after its event_id: a leftover journal resolves at any
1407	            # startup by asking the ledger whether the event committed.
1408	            event = self.audit.new_event(
1409	                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT, key_id,
1410	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS, event_id=event_id,
1411	            )
1412	            journal_id, journal_path = self._new_provision_journal(event.event_id)
1413	            committed = False
1414	            adopted = []  # (provider, handle) pairs minted by this attempt
1415	            try:
1416	                versions = []
1417	                for ver in payload["versions"]:
1418	                    version_record, target = self._adopt_imported_version(
1419	                        ver, journal_path
1420	                    )
1421	                    versions.append(version_record)
1422	                    adopted.append((target, version_record.handle))
1423	                record = KeyRecord(
1424	                    key_id=key_id,
1425	                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
1426	                    label=payload["label"],
1427	                    versions=versions,
1428	                    current_version=payload["current_version"],
1429	                    status=payload["status"],
1430	                    reason=payload["reason"],
1431	                    operator=payload["operator"],
1432	                    revoked_at=payload["revoked_at"],
1433	                )
1434	                path = self._path_for(key_id)
1435	                # Conflict recheck only after every version validated and
1436	                # every provider call succeeded; nothing has been written.
1437	                existing = self._read_record(path)
1438	                if existing is not None:
1439	                    return IMPORT_CONFLICT, existing
1440	                # A failure here rolls the just-created file back inside
1441	                # _commit_mutation; the finally block then reconciles the
1442	                # minted handles and the provision journal.
1443	                self._commit_mutation(
1444	                    path, record, event, None,
1445	                    journal_id=journal_id,
1446	                    pre_commit=pre_commit,
1447	                )
1448	                committed = True
1449	                # The handles are owned by the new record and the durable
1450	                # success event makes the journal obsolete.
1451	                self.drop_provision_journal(journal_id)
1452	                return IMPORT_CREATED, record
1453	            finally:
1454	                if not committed:
1455	                    # Any non-commit exit (provider failure, malformed
1456	                    # material, refused conflict, aborted transaction):
1457	                    # delete every minted handle and drop the journal; the
1458	                    # durable journal is also the crash safety net for
1459	                    # handles this frame no longer knows about. A failed
1460	                    # delete keeps the journal for startup and turns the
1461	                    # answer into 503 instead of hiding the orphan.
1462	                    self._abort_provision(journal_id, adopted)
